# AERIS-10N (Nexus) vs 10X (Extended) — architecture comparison

**Provisional; modeled placeholders.** Generated by `matlab/aeris_compare.m`
(15,000 raids per variant, modeled RF chain on). Both variants at 10.5 GHz.

## The two architectures

| | AERIS-10N (Nexus) | AERIS-10X (Extended) |
|---|---|---|
| array | 8×16 patch | 32×16 slotted waveguide |
| transmit | ~1 W × 16 (16 W) | 10 W × 16 (160 W GaN) |
| coverage | fixed 90° sector (stare) | 360° mechanical rotation |
| design range | 3 km | 20 km |

## Head-to-head (15,000 raids each)

| metric | 10N | 10X | 10X vs 10N |
|---|---|---|---|
| reliable range (0.03 m²) | 1.78 km | 6.28 km | 3.5× better |
| revisit | 1.02 s | 4.00 s | 4× slower |
| confirmation rate | 73.1 % | 99.2 % | better |
| **warning met 300 s** | **54.3 %** | **71.6 %** | **+17 pts** |
| median warning | 376 s | 456 s | better |
| **avg power** | **98 W** | **411 W** | **4.2× worse** |
| **runtime (960 Wh)** | **9.8 h** | **2.3 h** | **1/4** |
| **node weight** | **27 lb** | **46 lb** | **1.7× worse** |
| **node cost** | **$6.2k** | **$21.9k** | **3.6× worse** |

## Reading it

**10X is the better sensor and the worse attritable node — both statements
are true and quantified.** Its 3.5× range advantage *survives* the 4× slower
rotation revisit: warning satisfaction is still +17 points, so it genuinely
sees and warns more, not just farther on paper. The cost is on every SWaP-C
axis at once — 4× the power, a quarter the endurance, 1.7× the weight, 3.6× the
cost.

The rotation is a real trade, not a flaw: 10X covers 360° from one site where
10N stares at 90°. One 10X replaces a *ring* of 10N for coverage — but revisits
each bearing only once per rotation, which is why a fast threat can slip a
sweep gap (the residual in its warning number).

## The decision is the mission, and the numbers make it

| mission | choose | why |
|---|---|---|
| distributed / expeditionary / MEU | **4× 10N** | $24.6k, 108 lb, 400 W total, 360° tiled, 10 h each, attritable — lose one and shrug |
| fixed high-value point defense, power on hand | **1× 10X** | 6 km / 360° / 99% detection, when SWaP and attritability are not the binding constraints |

This is the study's stance: **radar performance is one axis; for the
attritable-distributed mission the small node wins the axes that actually
matter (weight, power, cost, quantity, survivability).** The comparison does
not pick a winner — it hands the decision-maker the tradeoff on every axis.

## Caveats

- 10X SWaP-C is estimated (waveguide array, GaN, rotator, enclosure); 10N is
  CN0566-class priced from distributors. Both are provisional.
- Runtime is on the same single 960 Wh (24 V 40 Ah) pack for an apples-to-apples
  power comparison; matching 10N endurance on 10X would need ~4× the battery
  (~+60 lb), widening the weight gap further.
- The upgraded 10N (see `nexus_upgrade_path.md`) is a third option that closes
  much of the range gap at a fraction of the SWaP-C.
